title: Preserve timezone offsets when serializing DateTime to epoch seconds or milliseconds
answers: Why is timezone offset ignored when serializing datetime with ser_json_temporal set to seconds or milliseconds?
How to convert DateTime to epoch timestamp with timezone in pydantic-core datetime serializers?
Why does datetime serialization to seconds or milliseconds produce incorrect timestamps for timezone-aware datetimes?
body:
Symptom: Timezone offset is ignored when serializing timezone-aware datetime instances with ser_json_temporal set to 'seconds' or 'milliseconds'.
Root cause: pydantic-core/src/serializers/type_serializers/datetime_etc.rs:datetime_to_seconds and datetime_to_milliseconds calculated epoch seconds from dt.date without accounting for dt's timezone offset.
Fix pattern: Call dt.timestamp_tz() to get timezone-adjusted epoch seconds and add fractional subseconds from dt.time.microsecond.
Constraints: Applies when converting DateTime to numeric timestamps in seconds or milliseconds; does not apply to naive Date objects or string temporal modes.
applies: Serializing DateTime values to numeric seconds or milliseconds in pydantic-core
